title: One page as another's key, at every long overlap
question: Does any forward page-pair difference at a relative offset with at least 120 overlapping runes show exceptional symbol concentration?
reader_question: Do any two pages become unusually patterned when one is shifted and subtracted from the other?
summary: Across 331,908 page-pair alignments, the strongest difference concentration is exceeded or matched by 77 of 128 shuffled search maxima.
finding: Maximum IoC 0.04721080446 occurs for LP2-14 minus LP2-35 at lag-140 over 131 runes; global plus-one empirical comparison 77+1 over 128+1 =0.60465116.331,908 observed counts are independently verified, including 330,582 new nonzero-lag settings.
reader_finding: The strongest alignment, LP2-14 against LP2-35, is no stronger than results commonly found in shuffled pages: 77 of 128 shuffled searches matched or exceeded it.
reader_limit: Forward differences with overlap at least 120 runes and an IoC statistic only; this does not exclude general shared-key encryption.
limitations: 52 eligible pages from 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages; no shorter overlaps, page reversal, wraparound, repeated/skipped key symbols or additional cipher layer. Shuffles preserve whole-page frequencies rather than each overlap frequency. Shifted-copy controls do not measure sensitivity to unrelated plaintexts encrypted under one key.
next_steps: Any broader shared-keystream claim needs a statistic with demonstrated power for its proposed plaintext model; freeze shorter-overlap or reversed-page extensions separately.
